text:
marta: Quick check-in — proposing adding an NVMe-backed spill tier with optional LZ4 compression as a middle ground between host staging and remote page store. Tradeoffs below.
kevin: sounds interesting. main question: CPU cost for compression vs PCIe transfer latency?
jordan: Also how does this interact with existing eviction/lease flow? We don't want extra failure modes on hot paths.
marta: Agree. Rough sketch: when we evict a page from GPU VRAM -> we try host staging as today; if host pool pressure high and node has local NVMe, spill to NVMe compressed blob. Metadata kept in our residency map with tier tag.
sree: Can you paste the config snippet you imagine?
marta: Sure:
```
spill.tiers = ["host", "nvme_compressed", "remote_kv"]
spill.nvme_compressed.enabled = true
spill.nvme_compressed.compress = "lz4"
spill.nvme_compressed.max_async_ops = 8
spill.nvme_compressed.write_batch_bytes = 64KB
```
david: That write_batch_bytes seems small — we need to measure PCIe QD vs small IO overhead. Might want 256KB-1MB for throughput.
kevin: If we compress, chunk size matters. Small chunks -> high CPU inflate/decompress overhead; big chunks -> higher latency for single-page restore. Suggest variable chunking: group low-hotness pages into larger blobs, keep high-hotness pages in host staging.
jordan: How do we decide hotness? We already track recent-access counters and lease age. Could reuse that for placement policy.
marta: Yes — policy: if hot_score > HOT_THRESHOLD -> keep host or pin; if medium -> NVMe compressed; if cold -> remote_kv. Also prefer NVMe for sequential eviction streams to get compression ratios.
sree: Recovery semantics? If node crashes, NVMe blobs might be orphaned. Need a GC/epoch cleanup and write-ahead manifest so remote controller can recover mapping.
marta: plan: per-blob manifest in small manifest store on NVMe header + periodic upload of mapping to control plane. On startup, agent scans /nvme/spill/manifest-*. If manifests orphaned beyond epoch ttl, scheduler reclaims ranges.
david: Add checksums (xxhash64) per-chunk to avoid silent corruption. Also mark compressed vs raw in header.
kevin: What about interaction with allocator — pinned pages and partial eviction? If a blob contains multiple pages, and we need only one page, decompressing a whole blob could be wasteful.
marta: two approaches: (1) small chunked blobs aligned to page-size for random-access pages; (2) larger multi-page blobs for low-hotness compaction. We can pick per-blob layout based on hotness/streaming heuristic.
jordan: Prefetching: on inference path, if we see in-flight seq wants X pages, we can issue async decompress read-ahead from NVMe. Need backpressure and upper bound on outstanding decompress tasks so we don't starve cores.
sree: telemetry: emit per-spill latency, compress_ratio, cpu-ms-per-MB, bytes_saved, and rehydrate-latency P95/P99. That will help model cost vs benefit.
marta: Good. Also need allocator API additions: add SpillLocation enum {HOST, NVME_COMPRESSED, REMOTE} and methods: mark_spill(location, blob_id, chunk_offsets[]). Keep api minimal.
david: Security: encrypted NVMe pools require KMS integration or dm-crypt; ensure key rotation is possible and manifests are encrypted.
kevin: Performance TODOs: bench compress+PCIe write pipeline, measure decompression latency on our inference CPU cores, simulate mixed workload with small hot pages.
jordan: Implementation plan: prototype agent-side nvme writer + lz4 lib, add manifest writer, integrate into evictor as optional backend behind a feature flag. Then 1) perf microbench 2) canary on low-traffic hosts 3) metrics-driven roll.
marta: Ok will open RFC PR with config proto, manifest format, and allocator api diff. Flagging @sree for recovery/manifest review.
deploy-bot: created rfc/2026-nvme-spill-compression in repo; link: https://git.internal/r/2026-nvme-spill-compression
sree: Thanks — will review manifest and gc section. Also add failure injection tests for partial write and crash during compress.
marta: Great, I'll add test cases and schedule a follow-up next Tue. :+1:
